source.interpretation: Traditional Item.CRIT and explicit FailureMode.CRITF are probabilities of a failure being critical; 1 means certain critical and 0 means certain noncritical for the tested mission type. The manuals say an on-mission noncritical fault permits mission continuation, while maintenance can follow when the aircraft returns.

predeclared_native_acceptance: Each zero-criticality child differs from its accepted critical=1 control only in ProblemDescription.PDESC and the one specified CRIT or CRITF cell; all other 29 or 33 native tables stay identical. Both inputs round-trip all authored row-containing tables exactly.

Guarded session-0 SSH import/export/calc/report/checker exits zero, converter reports zero errors and only expected logging warning #108, SXO/log/report nonempty, and GUI PID 13340 persists. Raw closure hashes remain immutable.

The fixed seed must yield at least one traditional LRU or explicit FM-POS-A fault during a mission, corresponding to its accepted control. The first fault is expected near h9.8829. The native log must classify that child fault as noncritical and show the affected aircraft continuing to the scheduled h10 mission success, instead of the accepted control's critical-fault abort. No claim of matching later stochastic failure timestamps is made before observation.

For each route, the failure must still produce a traceable post-mission repair or replacement/CM chain and a ready aircraft at the 36-hour stop; source and report ledgers must reconcile failure and repair counts. A noncritical fault must not be silently treated as no fault.

Traditional LRU physical issue, repair and stock effects must reconcile separately from explicit FMID position-linked CM; the two routes are not assumed to share an inventory path. The second and third missions' outcomes and any later fault timings are observed and reported, not guessed.
A separate read-only reviewer must replay the source controls, exact parent-child diffs, sealed native evidence and event/report/terminal ledger without importing the author validator.
limits: One aircraft, fixed seed, ordinary 2-hour missions and 36-hour horizon, CRIT or CRITF exactly 0 versus accepted 1, one traditional LRU and one explicit position failure mode only.

This does not test fractional criticality, mission-specific MissionCriticalityItem or MissionCriticalityFailureMode overrides, PFF, SYACF, NCFTL escalation, multiple simultaneous faults, other seeds, GUI-only behavior or cross-engine parity.
Full D08, D09 and Issue #18 remain open.
